title: Research the CURRENT (2025-2026) state of migrating a Next.js 16 App Router app to TanStack Start...
objective:
Research the CURRENT (2025-2026) state of migrating a Next.js 16 App Router app to TanStack Start, Hono, and Bun. Repo context only: it is a React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind 4 trading dashboard (Next.js 16.3.0) that calls a FastAPI backend via REST + SSE. Do NOT edit files — research only.
Investigate:
1. TanStack Start production-readiness today: current version, what it runs on (Vinxi/Nitro), Router + server functions + SSR story, SSR streaming, middleware, data loading (loaders), how it compares to Next.js App Router for a data-heavy dashboard with charts (lightweight-charts) and SSE streams.
2. Hono as the server layer: current version, JSX/server components story, streaming, SSE/WebSocket support, middleware ecosystem, deployment targets (Bun, Node, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, edge), and whether it is typically used standalone or inside TanStack Start.
3. Bun as runtime: current version, Bun.serve, Bun as a Next.js-compatible runtime (can Bun run next dev / next start in 2026?), Bun vs Node for Hono performance benchmarks (requests/sec, cold start), known production issues (npm compat, native modules, node: compat gaps).
4. Migration evidence: official migration guides (TanStack Start from Next.js, Hono from Express/Next API routes), real-world blog posts/issue threads on migrating Next.js apps to TanStack Start or Hono+Bun in 2025-2026, common pain points (router differences, server functions model, file conventions, auth, i18n, image optimization, caching).
5. Anything about running SSE through Hono/TanStack Start and whether Bun handles long-lived connections well.
Return CONCISE findings with evidence: source links (official docs, GitHub issues, benchmarks, blog posts) with dates, exact package versions you verified, confidence level per finding, and gaps in the evidence. End with a recommended migration posture (full swap vs staged) based on what you found. Keep it under 900 words.

Recon the repo at /home/mariobgsp/Project/github/trading-suite (a Next.js 16 + FastAPI trading dashboard) to assess a migration to TanStack Start + Hono + Bun. Read-only — do NOT edit files.
Report:
1. Frontend surface: inventory src/app/ routes and pages, src/components/ (Shell, Sidebar, MarketChart, ui), and src/lib/ (api client, polling/SSE hooks). For each, note Next.js-specific APIs used (useSearchParams, server components, the use client directive, next/image, next/link, caching, revalidation, route handlers, middleware, env vars like NEXT_PUBLIC_*).
2. Config surface: what next.config.ts contains (rewrites/proxies to the FastAPI backend? images config? headers?), how the frontend reaches the backend (proxy vs direct URL, SSE endpoints used, polling intervals), and anything in tsconfig.json / postcss / eslint that ties to Next.
3. Deployment/ops: Dockerfile(s), docker-compose.yml, scripts/run.sh, scripts/import_history.sh — how the app is built and run today, what ports, how the backend is started, any nginx/proxy layer.
4. Migration blast radius: which files would break first if the Next app were swapped (everything importing next/*, layout conventions, route conventions), which are framework-agnostic (lib/api client, chart components, pure UI), and any tests that cover frontend behavior.
Give file paths with approximate line ranges and a rough LOC count per area. End with: which parts are framework-clean vs framework-locked, and the cheapest staging path (e.g., what would let the app run under Bun/Hono with the least change). Keep it under 900 words.

Research the PRACTICAL TRADEOFFS of three migration targets for a Next.js 16 trading dashboard (React 19, lightweight-charts, SSE from a FastAPI backend): (a) full swap to TanStack Start, (b) Hono+Bun replacing only the server/runtime while keeping React on top (e.g., Vite + TanStack Router + Hono), (c) staged: adopt Bun as runtime for Next.js first, then Hono as a thin API gateway in front of FastAPI, keep Next for UI. Do NOT edit files — research only.
Cover:
1. Migration cost and risk per option: breaking changes, router paradigm shift (file-based vs TanStack Router code-based routes), server function/data loading model, SSR streaming for a dashboard, image optimization and static assets, middleware/auth, caching and revalidation semantics.
2. SSE and long-lived connections: how each target handles Server-Sent Events (Bun.serve, Hono streamSSE, TanStack Start SSR), known buffering/proxy issues, and whether Bun is production-stable for many concurrent long-lived connections.
3. Ecosystem and maintenance: npm/registry compat of Bun, ecosystem maturity of TanStack Start vs Next vs plain Hono, hiring/docs/community size, deployment targets (Docker, VPS, serverless) for each, and bundle/build tooling (Vite vs Next compiler vs Nitro/Vinxi).
4. How to VALIDATE cheaply: what a pilot would look like (e.g., run bun next dev today, or port ONE page to Hono+TanStack Router, or use Hono as a proxy) and what success metrics would tell you the migration is worth it.
Compare the three options in a short table plus prose. Give source links with dates and confidence. End with a clear recommendation for a dashboard app that is client-heavy, chart-heavy, and already depends on a separate Python API. Keep it under 900 words.
